title: Generative Language Modeling for Antibody CDR Grafting and Alignment-driven De Novo Design
summary: Antibodies recognise their targets through hypervariable complementarity-determining regions (CDRs), which are interleaved with conserved frameworks in sequence space, making  de novo CDR design an infilling problem. Autoregressive models generate residues left-to-right, which precludes full framework context during CDR generation and conflates framework and CDR likelihoods, leaving no natural prompt–response interface for feedback to steer generation. We present GenCDR, a family of LLaMa-based autoregressive language models that read all frameworks as a conditioning prompt and generate all CDRs jointly as a variable-length response, making CDR likelihoods a clean, separable target for reward attribution. The family comprises  IgGenCDR ,  p-IgGenCDR , and  NanoGenCDR , trained on unpaired, paired, and nanobody chains, respectively. GenCDR achieves the highest CDR recovery among autoregressive models and produces natural, diverse, human-like CDRs whose likelihoods correlate with fitness and developability assays. The prompt–response boundary also enables principled alignment: reward signals for binding affinity, expression, or developability can be composed to steer CDR generation. Over four rounds of alignment against antibody–antigen co-folding and developability objectives, we find that NanoGenCDR, which uses no explicit antigen encoding, can reach  in silico structural interface metrics competitive with those of a structure-conditioned diffusion pipeline at roughly half the sampling budget, with more natural, developable designs. The same interface can be extended to integrate experimental feedback, opening a path to closed-loop antibody  de novo design.

title: De novo design of allosterically controlled enzymes
summary: The ability of enzymes to sense signals and respond by changing their structure and activity underlies cellular processes from signaling to metabolic control. While there have been recent advances in the de novo design of enzymes and conformationally switching proteins, combining these to achieve allosteric regulation of enzymatic activity in a fully designed system remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we show that denoising diffusion models enable the design of compact de novo enzymes whose activity can be allosterically activated or repressed by designed protein effectors. Our results establish a general route to allosteric control over a wide range of catalytic and other protein functions.

AI.tldr: 디노이징 확산 모델(Denoising diffusion models)을 활용하여 설계된 단백질 이펙터에 의해 활성이 알로스테릭하게 활성화되거나 억제되는 신규 효소를 성공적으로 설계하였습니다.
AI.motivation: 신호 감지 및 구조 변화를 통한 효소 활성 조절(알로스테릭 조절)은 세포 내 대사 및 신호 전달의 핵심 기전이나, 완전한 신규 설계(de novo design) 시스템에서 효소의 촉매 활성과 입체 구조 전환을 결합하여 알로스테릭 조절을 구현하는 것은 여전히 어려운 과제로 남아 있었습니다.
AI.method: 디노이징 확산 모델(Denoising Diffusion Models)을 활용하여, 인공 설계된 단백질 이펙터(effector)와의 상호작용을 통해 알로스테릭 방식으로 활성화되거나 억제될 수 있는 소형(compact) 신규(de novo) 효소를 설계하였습니다.
AI.result: 설계된 단백질 작동체(effector)의 결합에 따라 효소의 활성이 알로스테릭하게 켜지거나(활성화) 꺼지는(억제) 정밀한 조절 능력을 갖춘 소형 신규 효소 시스템을 성공적으로 구현하였습니다.
AI.conclusion: 본 연구는 다양한 촉매 반응 및 단백질 기능에 대한 알로스테릭 제어를 가능하게 하는 범용적인 설계 접근법을 확립하였으며, 향후 합성생물학, 스마트 바이오센서 및 맞춤형 대사 제어 기술 개발에 크게 기여할 것으로 기대됩니다.
